name: Kubik AI LLM Content Generator (.md & llms.txt)
author: Kubik AI

sections.description:
Kubik AI converts real, fully rendered WordPress pages into clean, AI-ready Markdown endpoints that can be consumed by large language models, RAG pipelines, and AI-powered search tools.

Unlike traditional exporters that rely on raw post content, the plugin captures rendered HTML output, removes navigational noise, and produces structured Markdown optimized for machine understanding.

The built-in content index (llms.txt) provides a curated, human-readable map of your AI-ready content, with SEO-aware summaries and fine-grained control over what is exposed.

Features include:

  • Markdown output for pages at /slug.md
  • Optional Markdown output for posts
  • Automatic or manual llms.txt generation
  • Clean content extraction without theme layout
  • Removal of duplicate H1 headings
  • Conversion of links, headings and lists
  • Content summaries from SEO meta, excerpts or content
  • Admin settings with exclusions and search
  • Optional static llms.txt file generation

The plugin is designed for AI integration, dataset preparation and LLM-friendly content delivery.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu
  3. Open Settings → Kubik AI LLM Content Generator (.md & llms.txt)
  4. Select the content types to include
  5. Optionally exclude specific content by ID
  6. Generate llms.txt if a static file is required
sections.faq:
Does it support llms.txt standard?

Yes, it generates a structured llms.txt file for AI ingestion and indexing.

Why is /slug.md empty?

The page may not contain content inside standard containers. The plugin automatically falls back to the_content().

Can I enable posts?

Yes. Enable “Include posts” in the plugin settings.

Are taxonomies supported?

Yes. Public taxonomies can be included in llms.txt.

Does the plugin require ACF or SEO plugins?

No. Integration with ACF and AIOSEO is optional.

Does the plugin affect site performance?

No. Markdown output is generated on demand and can be cached.
